`CMakeLists.txt`:

```txt
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)
project(OpenCMR2 LANGUAGES C CXX)

# Targets (see CMakePresets.json):
#  - linux-x86: 32-bit x86, the reference build. The game's data structures
#    have the original's layout there, which the golden tests compare against.
#  - linux, windows-x64, macos: native 64-bit builds. Raw access review and
#    original-game parity checks are tracked in docs/64bit-raw-access.md.
#  - Android: built by the Gradle project in android/, which passes the NDK
#    toolchain and the SDL3 source it also takes SDLActivity from.

# The game source needs Clang with GNU-style options: -fms-extensions for the
# MSVC dialect it was written in, forced includes and the semantics below.
# On Windows that is clang++ (not clang-cl) targeting the MSVC runtime.
if(NOT CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID MATCHES "Clang" OR NOT CMAKE_C_COMPILER_ID MATCHES "Clang")
    message(FATAL_ERROR "OpenCMR2 builds with Clang (found ${CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID}); use one of the CMake presets")
endif()
if(CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_FRONTEND_VARIANT STREQUAL "MSVC")
    message(FATAL_ERROR "Use clang++, not clang-cl: the build passes GNU-style options")
endif()

option(OPENCMR2_SANITIZE "Build with AddressSanitizer and UBSan" OFF)
option(OPENCMR2_VENDORED_SDL "Download and build SDL3 instead of using an installed one" ${ANDROID})

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD 99)
set(CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS ON)

# Semantics the decompiled code relies on:
#  - signed overflow wraps (16.16 fixed point overflows on purpose);
#  - type punning through casts (the code was written against MSVC6);
#  - plain char is signed, as in MSVC (it is unsigned on ARM Linux);
#  - no fused multiply-add: the original rounds every product, and ARM64
#    compilers would otherwise fuse a * b + c and change physics results;
#  - explicit float stores use single precision, doubles use double precision;
#    the original's x87 nearest-even integer conversions are written explicitly
#    at audited physics sites (ordinary C++ casts would truncate).
add_compile_options(-fwrapv -fno-strict-aliasing -fsigned-char -ffp-contract=off)
if(CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR MATCHES "x86|i[3-6]86|AMD64")
    add_compile_options(-msse2 -mfpmath=sse)
endif()
if(WIN32)
    # The MSVC runtime warns about its own POSIX names and "unsafe" functions.
    add_compile_definitions(_CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS _CRT_NONSTDC_NO_WARNINGS NOMINMAX)
endif()

if(OPENCMR2_SANITIZE)
    add_compile_options(-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer)
    add_link_options(-fsanitize=address,undefined)
endif()

if(NOT OPENCMR2_VENDORED_SDL)
    find_package(SDL3 3.4 CONFIG COMPONENTS SDL3-shared)
endif()
if(NOT TARGET SDL3::SDL3)
    message(STATUS "OpenCMR2: building SDL3 from source")
    set(OPENCMR2_BUILT_SDL ON)
    include(FetchContent)
    set(SDL_SHARED ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
    set(SDL_STATIC OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
    set(SDL_TEST_LIBRARY OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
    set(SDL_EXAMPLES OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
    FetchContent_Declare(SDL3
        GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL.git
        GIT_TAG release-3.4.18
        GIT_SHALLOW TRUE)
    FetchContent_MakeAvailable(SDL3)
endif()

add_subdirectory(src)

# The tests run on the build machine; the Android build is the game alone.
if(NOT ANDROID)
    enable_testing()
    add_subdirectory(tests)
endif()

```

# OpenCMR2

[![Build](https://github.com/pablocpas/OpenCMR2/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/pablocpas/OpenCMR2/actions/workflows/build.yml)

OpenCMR2 is a work-in-progress native port of **Colin McRae Rally 2.0** (PC, 2000)
to modern platforms, built on the [CMR2Decomp](https://github.com/pablocpas/CMR2Decomp)
decompilation. It runs the original game code natively on Linux, Windows,
macOS and Android. There is no emulation and no Wine or DirectX wrapper: DirectDraw,
Direct3D 7, DirectSound, DirectInput, DirectPlay and Bink are replaced with
SDL3, the SDL GPU API (Vulkan, Metal) and the port's own code.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c7322dc-576b-4fb0-8d6a-4d17de6fe17d

*Colin McRae Rally 2.0 running on Linux with OpenCMR2.*

> [!WARNING]
> This repository contains no game assets. You need your own copy of the
> original PC version of Colin McRae Rally 2.0 to play.

## Status

Everything tested so far works: the intro videos, the menus, the stages and
network races over LAN. The project is still in development, so you may find
bugs. If you do, please [report them](https://github.com/pablocpas/OpenCMR2/issues).
The game code follows CMR2Decomp, and its progress is brought into the port
as it is made.

| Platform | Architecture | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Linux | x86-64 | Plays stages and matches the original physics |
| Linux | i686 | Plays stages, reference build with the original memory layout |
| Linux | ARM64 | Builds and passes the tests, gameplay not yet tested |
| Windows | x86-64 | Plays stages and matches the original physics (tested under Wine) |
| macOS | ARM64 | Builds and passes the tests, gameplay not yet tested |
| Android | ARM64, x86-64 | Plays stages with on-screen controls (Android 10 or later, Vulkan) |

### Features

* Native SDL3 platform layer for windowing, input, audio and files, with saves
  and settings in the user directory
* SDL GPU renderer (Vulkan, Metal) reproducing the Direct3D 7 fixed-function
  pipeline in shaders
* Fullscreen on the desktop resolution or a resizable window, switched with
  Alt+Enter
* Keyboard, mouse and gamepads through SDL3, and on-screen controls on Android
* Bink intro and country videos with a built-in decoder
* Multiplayer over LAN and the internet using UDP instead of DirectPlay
* Folder dialog on first launch to locate the game installation
* Fixes for some original bugs, such as German in the language menu loading
  Spanish

The improvements of [SilentPatch](https://cookieplmonster.github.io/mods/colin-mcrae-rally-2/)
are built in as well:

* Widescreen resolutions up to the desktop resolution, with the correct
  perspective instead of a stretched picture
* Configurable field of view
* High and variable frame rates without changing the game speed or the
  physics, verified against the original game

## Approach

The game code in `game/` comes from CMR2Decomp and is kept as close to the
original as possible. Every change the port needs is marked with a `PORT:`
comment. The rest of the port (`src/`) implements the platform APIs the game
expects on top of SDL3.

Accuracy is tested against the original executable rather than assumed:

* The fixed-point helpers are compared with the original x87 assembly
* The startup math tables (16,896 entries) are compared with dumps from the
  original game
* 500 vehicle updates of a Finland stage, driven by recorded input, are
  compared field by field with the original game + SilentPatch at 30, 60,
  120, 144 and 240 FPS and at a variable frame rate. All of them match bit
  for bit ([details](docs/PHYSICS_PARITY.md)).

Graphical enhancements will be added one at a time and kept optional, so the
original look stays available.

## Running

Download the package for your platform from
[Releases](https://github.com/pablocpas/OpenCMR2/releases):

| Platform | Package |
| --- | --- |
| Windows x64 | `OpenCMR2-Windows-x64.zip` |
| Linux x86-64 | `OpenCMR2-Linux-x86_64.tar.gz` |
| Linux ARM64 | `OpenCMR2-Linux-arm64.tar.gz` |
| Linux 32-bit | `OpenCMR2-Linux-i686.tar.gz` |
| macOS (Apple silicon) | `OpenCMR2-macOS-arm64.zip` |
| Android | `OpenCMR2-Android.apk` |

Extract it and run `opencmr2`. On first launch, choose the folder of your PC
installation. The installation itself, a folder inside it or a parent folder
all work. The location is checked and remembered, and the game files stay
where they are.

If you have the CD or an ISO, install the game or extract it first: OpenCMR2
reads the installed folders (`Game`, `FrontEnd`, `Sounds`, ...).

On Android, install the APK and copy the installation folder to the
device first. On first launch, choose it in the system's folder picker: the
game files are copied into the app once (about 700 MB), as Android gives
apps no direct access to other folders. The on-screen controls press the
default keyboard keys, so they work in the menus and on the stages, and
hide while a gamepad is used, external or built into a handheld. Back pauses the game.

The Linux packages are built on Ubuntu 24.04 and need a distribution of
similar age or newer. The macOS package is not signed: after extracting it,
run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine OpenCMR2-macOS-arm64` once.

Command-line options:

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--data <dir>` | Use this game installation and skip the folder dialog |
| `--user-dir <dir>` | Keep saves, settings and logs in this directory |

The installation can also be set with the `OPENCMR2_DATA` environment variable
or `[paths] data` in `opencmr2.ini`, or copied into a `Data` folder next to the
executable, which is found without asking.

## Configuration

Settings are stored in `opencmr2.ini` in the user directory
(`~/.local/share/OpenCMR2/` on Linux,
`%APPDATA%\OpenCMR2\` on Windows; files from the older
`OpenCMR2/OpenCMR2` folder are moved there).
It is created with comments on first launch.

| Setting | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[video] fullscreen` | `1` | Fullscreen (`1`) or window (`0`), changed and saved by Alt+Enter |
| `[video] fov` | `70` | Field of view in degrees, 30 to 150 (70 is the original) |
| `[video] run_in_background` | `0` | Keep running when the window loses focus |
| `[install] language` | `English` | English, American, French, German, Italian, Spanish or Polish |
| `[install] sku` | `EUROPE` | Game edition: `EUROPE`, `AMERICA`, `POLAND` or `JAPAN` |
| `[install] menu_shortcut` | asked | Entry in the applications menu (Linux) or Start menu (Windows): `1` keeps it pointing at this copy, `0` removes it |
| `[net] ...` | | Network play, see [NETWORK.md](docs/NETWORK.md) |

## Building

OpenCMR2 builds with Clang, CMake 3.24+, Ninja and glslang, using the presets
in `CMakePresets.json`:

| Preset | Target |
| --- | --- |
| `linux` | Linux, 64-bit (x86-64 or ARM64) |
| `windows-x64` | Windows x64 (`clang++` with the MSVC runtime) |
| `macos` | macOS, Apple silicon |
| `linux-x86` | Linux, 32-bit x86 (reference build for the tests) |

OpenCMR2 needs SDL 3.4 or later. An installed SDL3 of that version is used;
otherwise CMake downloads and builds it and places it next to the executable
(to force this, pass `-DOPENCMR2_VENDORED_SDL=ON`). Start by cloning the repository:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/pablocpas/OpenCMR2.git
cd OpenCMR2
```

### Linux

Install the dependencies.

Fedora (SDL3-devel is used when it is 3.4 or later):

```sh
sudo dnf install clang cmake ninja-build glslang SDL3-devel
```

Ubuntu 24.04 or Debian, where SDL3 is built from source with these
development libraries:

```sh
sudo apt install clang cmake ninja-build glslang-tools pkg-config \
    libx11-dev libxext-dev libxrandr-dev libxcursor-dev libxi-dev libxss-dev libxtst-dev \
    libxkbcommon-dev libwayland-dev wayland-protocols libegl1-mesa-dev \
    libasound2-dev libpulse-dev libudev-dev libdbus-1-dev
```

Then build:

```sh
cmake --preset linux
cmake --build --preset linux
```

The executable is `build/linux/src/opencmr2`.

### macOS

```sh
brew install cmake ninja glslang sdl3
cmake --preset macos
cmake --build --preset macos
```

Metal needs MSL shaders, so the build fetches SPIRV-Cross to translate them
(or uses `spirv-cross` from the `PATH`).

### Windows

Install Visual Studio 2022 with its "C++ Clang tools" component (or LLVM),
Ninja and [glslang](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glslang/releases). From an
"x64 Native Tools" command prompt:

```bat
cmake --preset windows-x64
cmake --build --preset windows-x64
```

`clang-cl` is not supported, as the build uses GNU-style options. To
cross-build from Linux with LLVM-MinGW, see [WINDOWS.md](docs/WINDOWS.md).

### Android

The Gradle project in `android/` builds the same CMake project with the
Android NDK. It needs JDK 17 or later, the Android SDK (with `ANDROID_HOME`
set or `sdk.dir` in `android/local.properties`) and glslang on the `PATH`.
Gradle downloads SDL's source and fetches the NDK, CMake and SDK platform
when the SDK licences are accepted:

```sh
cd android
./gradlew assembleRelease
```

The APK is `android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk`. It is
signed with the release key given by `OPENCMR2_KEYSTORE`,
`OPENCMR2_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`, `OPENCMR2_KEY_ALIAS` and
`OPENCMR2_KEY_PASSWORD` (or the `opencmr2.keystore` Gradle properties), and
with the debug key otherwise.

### Tests

```sh
ctest --preset linux
```

The 32-bit `linux-x86` build keeps the original data layout and is the
reference for the tests against the original game. Its dependencies and
the rest of the development workflow are described in
[DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md).

`android/app/build.gradle.kts`:

```kts
import java.net.URI
import javax.inject.Inject

plugins {
    alias(libs.plugins.android.application)
    alias(libs.plugins.kotlin.compose)
}

// The SDL3 release the desktop builds fetch (GIT_TAG in the top CMakeLists.txt).
// Its source gives both libSDL3.so, built with the game, and SDLActivity.
val sdlVersion: String = providers.fileContents(rootProject.layout.projectDirectory.file("../CMakeLists.txt"))
    .asText.map { Regex("""GIT_TAG release-([0-9.]+)""").find(it)!!.groupValues[1] }.get()

abstract class FetchSdl : DefaultTask() {
    @get:Input abstract val version: Property<String>
    @get:OutputDirectory abstract val sourceDir: DirectoryProperty
    @get:OutputDirectory abstract val javaDir: DirectoryProperty
    @get:Inject abstract val archives: ArchiveOperations
    @get:Inject abstract val files: FileSystemOperations

    @TaskAction
    fun fetch() {
        val v = version.get()
        val archive = temporaryDir.resolve("SDL3-$v.tar.gz")
        URI("https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/releases/download/release-$v/SDL3-$v.tar.gz").toURL()
            .openStream().use { input -> archive.outputStream().use { input.copyTo(it) } }
        files.sync {
            from(archives.tarTree(archives.gzip(archive)))
            into(sourceDir)
            // Drop the archive's top directory, SDL3-<version>.
            eachFile { relativePath = RelativePath(true, *relativePath.segments.drop(1).toTypedArray()) }
            includeEmptyDirs = false
        }
        files.sync {
            from(sourceDir.dir("android-project/app/src/main/java"))
            into(javaDir)
        }
        archive.delete()
    }
}

val fetchSdl = tasks.register<FetchSdl>("fetchSdl") {
    version = sdlVersion
    sourceDir = layout.buildDirectory.dir("sdl/source")
    javaDir = layout.buildDirectory.dir("sdl/java")
}

// Version from git: the tag (v1.0.2-14-gabcdef) and the number of commits.
fun git(vararg args: String): String =
    providers.exec { commandLine("git", *args); isIgnoreExitValue = true }.standardOutput.asText.get().trim()

android {
    namespace = "io.github.pablocpas.opencmr2"
    compileSdk = 37
    ndkVersion = "30.0.16248370"

    defaultConfig {
        applicationId = "io.github.pablocpas.opencmr2"
        // Android 10: Vulkan 1.1 on every 64-bit device.
        minSdk = 29
        targetSdk = 37
        versionCode = git("rev-list", "--count", "HEAD").toIntOrNull() ?: 1
        versionName = git("describe", "--tags", "--always").removePrefix("v").ifEmpty { "dev" }

        ndk {
            abiFilters += listOf("arm64-v8a", "x86_64")
        }
        externalNativeBuild {
            cmake {
                arguments += listOf(
                    "-DFETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_SDL3=${layout.buildDirectory.dir("sdl/source").get().asFile.absolutePath}",
                    "-DANDROID_STL=c++_static",
                )
                targets += listOf("opencmr2", "SDL3-shared")
            }
        }
    }

    externalNativeBuild {
        cmake {
            path = file("../../CMakeLists.txt")
            version = "4.1.2"
        }
    }

    // Release signing from the environment (CI secrets) or ~/.gradle/gradle.properties;
    // without a keystore the release is signed with the debug key, so it still installs.
    signingConfigs {
        create("release") {
            val keystore = providers.gradleProperty("opencmr2.keystore")
                .orElse(providers.environmentVariable("OPENCMR2_KEYSTORE")).orNull
            if (keystore != null) {
                storeFile = file(keystore)
                storePassword = providers.gradleProperty("opencmr2.keystore.password")
                    .orElse(providers.environmentVariable("OPENCMR2_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD")).orNull
                keyAlias = providers.gradleProperty("opencmr2.key.alias")
                    .orElse(providers.environmentVariable("OPENCMR2_KEY_ALIAS")).orNull
                keyPassword = providers.gradleProperty("opencmr2.key.password")
                    .orElse(providers.environmentVariable("OPENCMR2_KEY_PASSWORD")).orNull
            }
        }
    }

    buildTypes {
        release {
            isMinifyEnabled = true
            isShrinkResources = true
            proguardFiles(getDefaultProguardFile("proguard-android-optimize.txt"), "proguard-rules.pro")
            val release = signingConfigs.getByName("release")
            signingConfig = if (release.storeFile != null) release else signingConfigs.getByName("debug")
        }
    }

    buildFeatures {
        compose = true
    }

    // The app follows the system language, and Android 13+ lists these
    // languages in its per-app language settings (from res/values-*).
    // Library strings in other languages are left out, so a screen never
    // mixes languages.
    androidResources {
        generateLocaleConfig = true
        localeFilters += listOf("en", "de", "es", "fr", "it", "pl")
    }

    compileOptions {
        sourceCompatibility = JavaVersion.VERSION_17
        targetCompatibility = JavaVersion.VERSION_17
    }
}

androidComponents {
    onVariants { variant ->
        variant.sources.java?.addGeneratedSourceDirectory(fetchSdl, FetchSdl::javaDir)
    }
}

// CMake reads SDL from the fetched source.
tasks.configureEach {
    if (name.startsWith("configureCMake") || name.startsWith("buildCMake"))
        dependsOn(fetchSdl)
}

dependencies {
    implementation(libs.androidx.core.ktx)
    implementation(libs.androidx.activity.compose)
    implementation(libs.androidx.lifecycle.viewmodel.compose)
    implementation(platform(libs.androidx.compose.bom))
    implementation(libs.androidx.compose.ui)
    implementation(libs.androidx.compose.material3)
    implementation(libs.androidx.compose.ui.tooling.preview)
    debugImplementation(libs.androidx.compose.ui.tooling)
    implementation(libs.kotlinx.coroutines.android)
    implementation(libs.radialgamepad) {
        // Only its build used the old Android extensions plugin.
        exclude(group = "org.jetbrains.kotlin", module = "kotlin-android-extensions-runtime")
    }
}

`android/app/src/main/kotlin/io/github/pablocpas/opencmr2/GameActivity.kt`:

```kt
package io.github.pablocpas.opencmr2

import android.os.Bundle
import android.view.KeyEvent
import android.view.MotionEvent
import org.libsdl.app.SDLActivity

/** The game: SDL runs SDL_main from libmain.so, with the on-screen controls over it. */
class GameActivity : SDLActivity() {
    private var controls: TouchControls? = null

    override fun getLibraries() = arrayOf("SDL3", "main")

    override fun getArguments() = arrayOf("--data", GameData.directory(this).absolutePath)

    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        // SDLActivity shows its own error when the libraries do not load.
        if (!mBrokenLibraries && mLayout != null)
            controls = TouchControls(this, mLayout)
    }

    // Back (the button or the gesture) is the game's Escape. Android sends its
    // press and release together; the game reads the keyboard once a frame,
    // so the release is held back long enough for it to see the press.
    override fun dispatchKeyEvent(event: KeyEvent): Boolean {
        controls?.onInput(event.source)
        if (event.keyCode != KeyEvent.KEYCODE_BACK || mBrokenLibraries)
            return super.dispatchKeyEvent(event)
        if (event.action == KeyEvent.ACTION_DOWN && event.repeatCount == 0) {
            onNativeKeyDown(KeyEvent.KEYCODE_ESCAPE)
            window.decorView.postDelayed({ onNativeKeyUp(KeyEvent.KEYCODE_ESCAPE) }, 100)
        }
        return true
    }

    override fun dispatchTouchEvent(event: MotionEvent): Boolean {
        controls?.onInput(event.source)
        return super.dispatchTouchEvent(event)
    }

    override fun dispatchGenericMotionEvent(event: MotionEvent): Boolean {
        controls?.onInput(event.source)
        return super.dispatchGenericMotionEvent(event)
    }

    override fun onPause() {
        controls?.releaseAll()
        super.onPause()
    }

    override fun onDestroy() {
        controls?.close()
        controls = null
        super.onDestroy()
    }
}

`android/app/src/main/kotlin/io/github/pablocpas/opencmr2/GameData.kt`:

```kt
package io.github.pablocpas.opencmr2

import android.content.ContentResolver
import android.content.Context
import android.net.Uri
import android.os.StatFs
import android.provider.DocumentsContract
import android.provider.DocumentsContract.Document
import kotlinx.coroutines.ensureActive
import java.io.File
import java.io.IOException
import kotlin.coroutines.coroutineContext

/**
 * The copy of the PC game the app plays: an installation copied into the
 * app's storage, read by the game with ordinary file access. Android gives
 * apps no such access to a folder the player chooses, so the import copies it
 * from there once (Storage Access Framework), as other ports of PC games do.
 */
object GameData {
    // Files every PC edition has; the check MissingGameData does in src/platform/sys.cpp.
    private val REQUIRED = listOf("Game/Bigfiles/common.bfl", "FrontEnd/common.bfl", "Sounds/surface.bfl")

    private fun storage(context: Context): File = context.getExternalFilesDir(null) ?: context.filesDir

    /** Where the game data lives; passed to the game with --data. */
    fun directory(context: Context): File = File(storage(context), "game")

    fun isInstalled(context: Context): Boolean {
        val dir = directory(context)
        return REQUIRED.all { path ->
            val file = path.split('/').fold<String, File?>(dir) { parent, name ->
                parent?.listFiles()?.firstOrNull { it.name.equals(name, ignoreCase = true) }
            }
            file != null && file.isFile && file.length() > 0
        }
    }

    sealed interface Progress {
        data object Searching : Progress
        data class Copying(val copied: Long, val total: Long) : Progress
    }

    sealed class ImportException(message: String) : IOException(message) {
        class NotFound : ImportException("No installation found")
        class Ambiguous(val folders: List<String>) : ImportException("More than one installation found")
        class NoSpace(val needed: Long, val available: Long) : ImportException("Not enough space")
    }

    /**
     * Copies the installation in or under [tree] (a folder from
     * ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT_TREE) to [directory]. The copy goes to a temporary
     * folder first, so an interrupted import leaves nothing half done.
     */
    suspend fun import(context: Context, tree: Uri, onProgress: (Progress) -> Unit) {
        onProgress(Progress.Searching)
        val source = DocumentTree(context.contentResolver, tree)
        val found = source.findInstallations()
        val root = when (found.size) {
            0 -> throw ImportException.NotFound()
            1 -> found.single()
            else -> throw ImportException.Ambiguous(found.map { it.path })
        }
        val files = source.listFiles(root.documentId)
        val total = files.sumOf { it.second.size }

        val target = directory(context)
        val temporary = File(storage(context), "game.import")
        temporary.deleteRecursively()
        // The space of an earlier copy is freed when this one replaces it.
        val available = StatFs(storage(context).path).availableBytes + target.walkBottomUp().sumOf { it.length() }
        val margin = 64L shl 20
        if (available < total + margin)
            throw ImportException.NoSpace(total + margin, available)

        try {
            var copied = 0L
            var reported = 0L
            val buffer = ByteArray(1 shl 20)
            onProgress(Progress.Copying(0, total))
            for ((path, entry) in files) {
                val file = File(temporary, path)
                file.parentFile!!.mkdirs()
                source.open(entry.documentId).use { input ->
                    file.outputStream().use { output ->
                        while (true) {
                            coroutineContext.ensureActive()
                            val n = input.read(buffer)
                            if (n < 0) break
                            output.write(buffer, 0, n)
                            copied += n
                            if (copied - reported >= (4 shl 20)) {
                                onProgress(Progress.Copying(copied, total))
                                reported = copied
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            onProgress(Progress.Copying(total, total))
            target.deleteRecursively()
            if (!temporary.renameTo(target))
                throw IOException("Cannot move the copied files to $target")
        } finally {
            temporary.deleteRecursively()
        }
    }

    private class DocumentTree(private val resolver: ContentResolver, private val tree: Uri) {
        data class Entry(val documentId: String, val name: String, val isDirectory: Boolean, val size: Long)
        data class Folder(val documentId: String, val path: String)

        fun children(documentId: String): List<Entry> {
            val uri = DocumentsContract.buildChildDocumentsUriUsingTree(tree, documentId)
            val projection = arrayOf(
                Document.COLUMN_DOCUMENT_ID, Document.COLUMN_DISPLAY_NAME, Document.COLUMN_MIME_TYPE, Document.COLUMN_SIZE,
            )
            val entries = mutableListOf<Entry>()
            resolver.query(uri, projection, null, null, null)?.use { cursor ->
                while (cursor.moveToNext()) {
                    entries += Entry(
                        documentId = cursor.getString(0),
                        name = cursor.getString(1) ?: continue,
                        isDirectory = cursor.getString(2) == Document.MIME_TYPE_DIR,
                        size = if (cursor.isNull(3)) 0 else cursor.getLong(3),
                    )
                }
            }
            return entries
        }

        fun open(documentId: String) =
            resolver.openInputStream(DocumentsContract.buildDocumentUriUsingTree(tree, documentId))
                ?: throw IOException("Cannot open $documentId")

        private fun isInstallation(documentId: String): Boolean = REQUIRED.all { path ->
            var entry: Entry? = null
            var parent = documentId
            for (name in path.split('/')) {
                entry = children(parent).firstOrNull { it.name.equals(name, ignoreCase = true) } ?: return@all false
                parent = entry.documentId
            }
            entry != null && !entry.isDirectory && entry.size > 0
        }

        /**
         * The chosen folder when it is an installation, otherwise the ones
         * found up to three levels below it (a download folder around it, as
         * on the desktop). Found installations are not searched further.
         */
        fun findInstallations(): List<Folder> {
            val pending = ArrayDeque(listOf(Folder(DocumentsContract.getTreeDocumentId(tree), "") to 0))
            val found = mutableListOf<Folder>()
            var visited = 0
            while (pending.isNotEmpty() && visited++ < 512) {
                val (folder, depth) = pending.removeFirst()
                if (isInstallation(folder.documentId)) {
                    found += folder
                    continue
                }
                if (depth == 3) continue
                for (child in children(folder.documentId)) {
                    if (child.isDirectory && !child.name.startsWith('.'))
                        pending += Folder(child.documentId, folder.path + "/" + child.name) to depth + 1
                }
            }
            return found
        }

        /** Every file under the folder, with its path relative to it. */
        fun listFiles(documentId: String): List<Pair<String, Entry>> {
            val files = mutableListOf<Pair<String, Entry>>()
            fun walk(id: String, prefix: String) {
                for (child in children(id)) {
                    if (child.isDirectory) walk(child.documentId, prefix + child.name + "/")
                    else files += prefix + child.name to child
                }
            }
            walk(documentId, "")
            return files
        }
    }
}

```kt
package io.github.pablocpas.opencmr2

import android.app.Application
import android.content.Intent
import android.net.Uri
import android.os.Bundle
import android.text.format.Formatter
import android.view.WindowManager
import androidx.activity.ComponentActivity
import androidx.activity.compose.rememberLauncherForActivityResult

import androidx.activity.result.contract.ActivityResultContracts
import androidx.compose.foundation.Image

import androidx.compose.material3.TextButton

import androidx.compose.material3.lightColorScheme
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable

import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color
import androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalContext
import androidx.compose.ui.res.painterResource
import androidx.compose.ui.res.stringResource
import androidx.compose.ui.text.style.TextAlign
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import androidx.lifecycle.AndroidViewModel
import androidx.lifecycle.viewModelScope
import androidx.lifecycle.viewmodel.compose.viewModel
import kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.Job
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.MutableStateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.StateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext

/** Starts the game, after importing the game files on the first launch. */
class SetupActivity : ComponentActivity() {
    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        if (GameData.isInstalled(this)) {
            startGame()
            return
        }
        enableEdgeToEdge()
        setContent {
            SetupTheme {
                val model: SetupViewModel = viewModel()
                val state by model.state.collectAsState()
                // Keep the screen on while copying: the import stops if the app is closed.
                LaunchedEffect(state is SetupState.Working) {
                    if (state is SetupState.Working) window.addFlags(WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON)
                    else window.clearFlags(WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON)
                }
                LaunchedEffect(state) {
                    if (state is SetupState.Done) startGame()
                }
                SetupScreen(state, onFolderChosen = model::import, onCancel = model::cancel)
            }
        }
    }

    private fun startGame() {
        startActivity(Intent(this, GameActivity::class.java))
        finish()
    }
}

sealed interface SetupState {
    data object Welcome : SetupState
    data class Working(val progress: GameData.Progress) : SetupState
    data class Failed(val error: Throwable) : SetupState
    data object Done : SetupState
}

class SetupViewModel(application: Application) : AndroidViewModel(application) {
    private val _state = MutableStateFlow<SetupState>(SetupState.Welcome)
    val state: StateFlow<SetupState> = _state
    private var job: Job? = null

    fun import(tree: Uri) {
        if (job?.isActive == true) return
        job = viewModelScope.launch {
            _state.value = try {
                withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
                    GameData.import(getApplication(), tree) { _state.value = SetupState.Working(it) }
                }
                SetupState.Done
            } catch (e: CancellationException) {
                SetupState.Welcome
            } catch (e: Exception) {
                SetupState.Failed(e)
            }
        }
    }

    fun cancel() {
        job?.cancel()
    }
}

@Composable
private fun SetupTheme(content: @Composable () -> Unit) {
    val accent = Color(0xFF01899D)
    val colors = if (isSystemInDarkTheme()) darkColorScheme(primary = Color(0xFF5CD5EA))
                 else lightColorScheme(primary = accent)
    MaterialTheme(colorScheme = colors) {
        Surface(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize(), content = content)
    }
}

@Composable
private fun SetupScreen(state: SetupState, onFolderChosen: (Uri) -> Unit, onCancel: () -> Unit) {
    val chooser = rememberLauncherForActivityResult(ActivityResultContracts.OpenDocumentTree()) { uri ->
        if (uri != null) onFolderChosen(uri)
    }
    Box(
        modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize().safeDrawingPadding().verticalScroll(rememberScrollState()),
        contentAlignment = Alignment.Center,
    ) {
        Column(
            modifier = Modifier.widthIn(max = 560.dp).fillMaxWidth().padding(24.dp),
            horizontalAlignment = Alignment.CenterHorizontally,
            verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(16.dp),
        ) {
            Image(
                painter = painterResource(R.drawable.logo),
                contentDescription = null,
                modifier = Modifier.size(96.dp).clip(RoundedCornerShape(24.dp)),
            )
            Text(stringResource(R.string.setup_title), style = MaterialTheme.typography.headlineMedium)
            when (state) {
                SetupState.Welcome, SetupState.Done -> {
                    Text(stringResource(R.string.setup_intro), textAlign = TextAlign.Center)
                    Text(
                        stringResource(R.string.setup_where),
                        style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall,
                        textAlign = TextAlign.Center,
                    )
                    Button(onClick = { chooser.launch(null) }) { Text(stringResource(R.string.setup_choose)) }
                }
                is SetupState.Working -> Working(state.progress, onCancel)
                is SetupState.Failed -> {
                    Text(
                        errorText(state.error),
                        color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.error,
                        textAlign = TextAlign.Center,
                    )
                    Button(onClick = { chooser.launch(null) }) { Text(stringResource(R.string.setup_choose_again)) }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

@Composable
private fun Working(progress: GameData.Progress, onCancel: () -> Unit) {
    val context = LocalContext.current
    when (progress) {
        GameData.Progress.Searching -> {
            Text(stringResource(R.string.setup_searching))
            LinearProgressIndicator(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth())
        }
        is GameData.Progress.Copying -> {
            Text(
                stringResource(
                    R.string.setup_copying,
                    Formatter.formatShortFileSize(context, progress.copied),
                    Formatter.formatShortFileSize(context, progress.total),
                )
            )
            LinearProgressIndicator(
                progress = { if (progress.total > 0) progress.copied.toFloat() / progress.total else 0f },
                modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
            )
        }
    }
    TextButton(onClick = onCancel) { Text(stringResource(android.R.string.cancel)) }
}

@Composable
private fun errorText(error: Throwable): String {
    val context = LocalContext.current
    return when (error) {
        is GameData.ImportException.NotFound -> stringResource(R.string.setup_not_found)
        is GameData.ImportException.Ambiguous ->
            stringResource(R.string.setup_ambiguous, error.folders.take(4).joinToString("\n") { "• " + it.ifEmpty { "/" } })
        is GameData.ImportException.NoSpace -> stringResource(
            R.string.setup_no_space,
            Formatter.formatShortFileSize(context, error.needed),
            Formatter.formatShortFileSize(context, error.available),
        )
        else -> stringResource(R.string.setup_failed, error.localizedMessage ?: error.toString())
    }
}

`android/app/src/main/kotlin/io/github/pablocpas/opencmr2/TouchControls.kt`:

```kt
package io.github.pablocpas.opencmr2

import android.app.Activity
import android.content.Context
import android.hardware.input.InputManager
import android.os.Handler
import android.os.Looper
import android.view.Gravity
import android.view.InputDevice
import android.view.KeyEvent
import android.view.ViewGroup
import android.widget.FrameLayout
import androidx.core.view.ViewCompat
import androidx.core.view.WindowInsetsCompat
import androidx.core.view.isVisible
import com.swordfish.radialgamepad.library.RadialGamePad
import com.swordfish.radialgamepad.library.config.ButtonConfig
import com.swordfish.radialgamepad.library.config.CrossConfig
import com.swordfish.radialgamepad.library.config.PrimaryDialConfig
import com.swordfish.radialgamepad.library.config.RadialGamePadConfig
import com.swordfish.radialgamepad.library.config.RadialGamePadTheme
import com.swordfish.radialgamepad.library.config.SecondaryDialConfig
import com.swordfish.radialgamepad.library.event.Event
import kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.MainScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.cancel
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch
import org.libsdl.app.SDLActivity

/**
 * On-screen controls drawn over the game with RadialGamePad. They press the
 * keys of the game's default keyboard layout for player 1, so they work in the
 * menus and on the stages without setting up a controller: arrows steer,
 * accelerate and brake (and move through the menus), Space is the handbrake,
 * ] and [ change gear, C the camera, Enter and Escape confirm and pause.
 * They hide while a gamepad is played and come back on a touch.
 */
class TouchControls(private val activity: Activity, parent: ViewGroup) : InputManager.InputDeviceListener {
    private val scope: CoroutineScope = MainScope()
    private val inputManager = activity.getSystemService(Context.INPUT_SERVICE) as InputManager
    private val pressed = mutableSetOf<Int>()
    private val overlay = FrameLayout(activity)

    init {
        val theme = RadialGamePadTheme(
            normalColor = 0x50FFFFFF,
            pressedColor = 0xA0FFFFFF.toInt(),
            textColor = 0xE0FFFFFF.toInt(),
            backgroundColor = 0x28000000,
            lightColor = 0x30FFFFFF,
        )
        val left = RadialGamePad(leftConfig(theme), 8f, activity)
        val right = RadialGamePad(rightConfig(theme), 8f, activity)
        for ((pad, gravity) in listOf(left to (Gravity.BOTTOM or Gravity.START), right to (Gravity.BOTTOM or Gravity.END))) {
            overlay.addView(pad, FrameLayout.LayoutParams(0, 0, gravity))
            scope.launch { pad.events().collect(::handle) }
        }
        // Each pad takes about half the screen height, clear of display cutouts.
        overlay.addOnLayoutChangeListener { _, l, t, r, b, _, _, _, _ ->
            val size = (minOf(r - l, b - t) * 0.55f).toInt()
            for (pad in listOf(left, right)) {
                val params = pad.layoutParams
                if (params.width != size) {
                    params.width = size
                    params.height = size
                    pad.post { pad.layoutParams = params }
                }
            }
        }
        ViewCompat.setOnApplyWindowInsetsListener(overlay) { view, insets ->
            val cutout = insets.getInsets(WindowInsetsCompat.Type.displayCutout())
            view.setPadding(cutout.left, cutout.top, cutout.right, cutout.bottom)
            insets
        }
        parent.addView(overlay, ViewGroup.LayoutParams(ViewGroup.LayoutParams.MATCH_PARENT, ViewGroup.LayoutParams.MATCH_PARENT))

        inputManager.registerInputDeviceListener(this, Handler(Looper.getMainLooper()))
        updateVisibility()
    }

    private fun leftConfig(theme: RadialGamePadTheme) = RadialGamePadConfig(
        sockets = 12,
        primaryDial = PrimaryDialConfig.Cross(CrossConfig(id = CROSS, useDiagonals = false)),
        secondaryDials = listOf(
            SecondaryDialConfig.Empty(index = 1, spread = 1, scale = 1f, distance = 0f),
            button(index = 2, KeyEvent.KEYCODE_ESCAPE, R.drawable.ic_touch_pause, R.string.touch_pause),
            SecondaryDialConfig.Empty(index = 3, spread = 1, scale = 1f, distance = 0f),
        ),
        theme = theme,
    )

    private fun rightConfig(theme: RadialGamePadTheme) = RadialGamePadConfig(
        sockets = 12,
        // Counterclockwise from the right: Enter, accelerate, handbrake, brake.
        primaryDial = PrimaryDialConfig.PrimaryButtons(
            dials = listOf(
                ButtonConfig(KeyEvent.KEYCODE_ENTER, iconId = R.drawable.ic_touch_ok,
                    contentDescription = activity.getString(R.string.touch_ok)),
                ButtonConfig(KeyEvent.KEYCODE_DPAD_UP, iconId = R.drawable.ic_touch_accelerate,
                    contentDescription = activity.getString(R.string.touch_accelerate)),
                ButtonConfig(KeyEvent.KEYCODE_SPACE, iconId = R.drawable.ic_touch_handbrake,
                    contentDescription = activity.getString(R.string.touch_handbrake)),
                ButtonConfig(KeyEvent.KEYCODE_DPAD_DOWN, iconId = R.drawable.ic_touch_brake,
                    contentDescription = activity.getString(R.string.touch_brake)),
            ),
            allowMultiplePressesSingleFinger = false,
        ),
        secondaryDials = listOf(
            button(index = 3, KeyEvent.KEYCODE_RIGHT_BRACKET, R.drawable.ic_touch_gear_up, R.string.touch_gear_up),
            button(index = 4, KeyEvent.KEYCODE_LEFT_BRACKET, R.drawable.ic_touch_gear_down, R.string.touch_gear_down),
            button(index = 5, KeyEvent.KEYCODE_C, R.drawable.ic_touch_camera, R.string.touch_camera),
        ),
        theme = theme,
    )

    private fun button(index: Int, keyCode: Int, icon: Int, description: Int) = SecondaryDialConfig.SingleButton(
        index = index,
        scale = 1f,
        distance = 0f,
        buttonConfig = ButtonConfig(keyCode, iconId = icon, contentDescription = activity.getString(description)),
    )

    private fun handle(event: Event) {
        when (event) {
            is Event.Button -> set(event.id, event.action == KeyEvent.ACTION_DOWN)
            is Event.Direction -> {
                // The cross has no diagonals: one direction at a time, y down.
                set(KeyEvent.KEYCODE_DPAD_LEFT, event.xAxis < -0.5f)
                set(KeyEvent.KEYCODE_DPAD_RIGHT, event.xAxis > 0.5f)
                set(KEYCODE_CROSS_UP, event.yAxis < -0.5f)
                set(KEYCODE_CROSS_DOWN, event.yAxis > 0.5f)
            }
        }
    }

    // The cross and the right pad both press Up and Down; each keeps its own
    // state, and the key is down while either holds it.
    private fun set(id: Int, down: Boolean) {
        val wasDown = keyDown(keyOf(id))
        if (down) pressed += id else pressed -= id
        val isDown = keyDown(keyOf(id))
        if (isDown != wasDown) {
            if (isDown) SDLActivity.onNativeKeyDown(keyOf(id)) else SDLActivity.onNativeKeyUp(keyOf(id))
        }
    }

    private fun keyDown(keyCode: Int) = pressed.any { keyOf(it) == keyCode }

    private fun keyOf(id: Int) = when (id) {
        KEYCODE_CROSS_UP -> KeyEvent.KEYCODE_DPAD_UP
        KEYCODE_CROSS_DOWN -> KeyEvent.KEYCODE_DPAD_DOWN
        else -> id
    }

    /** Lets go of every key, when the game pauses or the controls hide. */
    fun releaseAll() {
        for (id in pressed.toList()) set(id, false)
    }

    // A controller, external or built into a handheld, has gamepad buttons.
    // Phones list other built-in devices with joystick sources too (the
    // OnePlus 12's touch panel), but those have no gamepad buttons.
    private fun isGamepad(device: InputDevice?) = device != null && !device.isVirtual &&
        device.supportsSource(InputDevice.SOURCE_GAMEPAD) && !device.supportsSource(InputDevice.SOURCE_TOUCHSCREEN)

    private fun show(visible: Boolean) {
        if (!visible) releaseAll()
        overlay.isVisible = visible
    }

    private fun updateVisibility() =
        show(inputManager.inputDeviceIds.none { isGamepad(inputManager.getInputDevice(it)) })

    /**
     * Follows what is being played, by the source of each event: a gamepad
     * button or stick hides the controls, a touch shows them again.
     */
    fun onInput(source: Int) {
        if ((source and InputDevice.SOURCE_TOUCHSCREEN) == InputDevice.SOURCE_TOUCHSCREEN) {
            if (!overlay.isVisible) show(true)
        } else if (overlay.isVisible && ((source and InputDevice.SOURCE_GAMEPAD) == InputDevice.SOURCE_GAMEPAD ||
                (source and InputDevice.SOURCE_JOYSTICK) == InputDevice.SOURCE_JOYSTICK)) {
            show(false)
        }
    }

    override fun onInputDeviceAdded(deviceId: Int) = updateVisibility()
    override fun onInputDeviceRemoved(deviceId: Int) = updateVisibility()
    override fun onInputDeviceChanged(deviceId: Int) {}

    fun close() {
        releaseAll()
        inputManager.unregisterInputDeviceListener(this)
        scope.cancel()
        (overlay.parent as? ViewGroup)?.removeView(overlay)
    }

    private companion object {
        const val CROSS = -1
        // Ids of the cross's up and down, which press the same keys as the right pad.
        const val KEYCODE_CROSS_UP = -2
        const val KEYCODE_CROSS_DOWN = -3
    }
}

        <exclude domain="external" path="game/" />
        <exclude domain="external" path="game.import/" />
    </cloud-backup>
    <device-transfer>
        <exclude domain="external" path="game/" />
        <exclude domain="external" path="game.import/" />
    </device-transfer>
</data-extraction-rules>

`android/gradlew`:

```
#!/bin/sh

#
# Copyright © 2015 the original authors.
#
# Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
# you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
# You may obtain a copy of the License at
#
#      https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
#
# Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
# distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
# WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
# See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
# limitations under the License.
#
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
#

##############################################################################
#
#   gradlew start up script for POSIX generated by Gradle.
#
#   Important for running:
#
#   (1) You need a POSIX-compliant shell to run this script. If your /bin/sh is
#       noncompliant, but you have some other compliant shell such as ksh or
#       bash, then to run this script, type that shell name before the whole
#       command line, like:
#
#           ksh gradlew
#
#       Busybox and similar reduced shells will NOT work, because this script
#       requires all of these POSIX shell features:
#         * functions;
#         * expansions «$var», «${var}», «${var:-default}», «${var+SET}»,
#           «${var#prefix}», «${var%suffix}», and «$( cmd )»;
#         * compound commands having a testable exit status, especially «case»;
#         * various built-in commands including «command», «set», and «ulimit».
#
#   Important for patching:
#
#   (2) This script targets any POSIX shell, so it avoids extensions provided
#       by Bash, Ksh, etc; in particular arrays are avoided.
#
#       The "traditional" practice of packing multiple parameters into a
#       space-separated string is a well documented source of bugs and security
#       problems, so this is (mostly) avoided, by progressively accumulating
#       options in "$@", and eventually passing that to Java.
#
#       Where the inherited environment variables (DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS,
#       and GRADLE_OPTS) rely on word-splitting, this is performed explicitly;
#       see the in-line comments for details.
#
#       There are tweaks for specific operating systems such as AIX, CygWin,
#       Darwin, MinGW, and NonStop.
#
#   (3) This script is generated from the Groovy template
#       https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/3d91ce3b8caaf77ad09f381f43615b715b53f72c/platforms/jvm/plugins-application/src/main/resources/org/gradle/api/internal/plugins/unixStartScript.txt
#       within the Gradle project.
#
#       You can find Gradle at https://github.com/gradle/gradle/.
#
##############################################################################

# Attempt to set APP_HOME

# Resolve links: $0 may be a link
app_path=$0

# Need this for daisy-chained symlinks.
while
    APP_HOME=${app_path%"${app_path##*/}"}  # leaves a trailing /; empty if no leading path
    [ -h "$app_path" ]
do
    ls=$( ls -ld "$app_path" )
    link=${ls#*' -> '}
    case $link in             #(
      /*)   app_path=$link ;; #(
      *)    app_path=$APP_HOME$link ;;
    esac
done

# This is normally unused
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
APP_BASE_NAME=${0##*/}
# Discard cd standard output in case $CDPATH is set (https://github.com/gradle/gradle/issues/25036)
APP_HOME=$( cd -P "${APP_HOME:-./}" > /dev/null && printf '%s\n' "$PWD" ) || exit

# Use the maximum available, or set MAX_FD != -1 to use that value.
MAX_FD=maximum

warn () {
    echo "$*"
} >&2

die () {
    echo
    echo "$*"
    echo
    exit 1
} >&2

# OS specific support (must be 'true' or 'false').
cygwin=false
msys=false
darwin=false
nonstop=false
case "$( uname )" in                #(
  CYGWIN* )         cygwin=true  ;; #(
  Darwin* )         darwin=true  ;; #(
  MSYS* | MINGW* )  msys=true    ;; #(
  NONSTOP* )        nonstop=true ;;
esac



# Determine the Java command to use to start the JVM.
if [ -n "$JAVA_HOME" ] ; then
    if [ -x "$JAVA_HOME/jre/sh/java" ] ; then
        # IBM's JDK on AIX uses strange locations for the executables
        JAVACMD=$JAVA_HOME/jre/sh/java
    else
        JAVACMD=$JAVA_HOME/bin/java
    fi
    if [ ! -x "$JAVACMD" ] ; then
        die "ERROR: JAVA_HOME is set to an invalid directory: $JAVA_HOME

Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the
location of your Java installation."
    fi
else
    JAVACMD=java
    if ! command -v java >/dev/null 2>&1
    then
        die "ERROR: JAVA_HOME is not set and no 'java' command could be found in your PATH.

Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the
location of your Java installation."
    fi
fi

# Increase the maximum file descriptors if we can.
if ! "$cygwin" && ! "$darwin" && ! "$nonstop" ; then
    case $MAX_FD in #(
      max*)
        # In POSIX sh, ulimit -H is undefined. That's why the result is checked to see if it worked.
        # shellcheck disable=SC2039,SC3045
        MAX_FD=$( ulimit -H -n ) ||
            warn "Could not query maximum file descriptor limit"
    esac
    case $MAX_FD in  #(
      '' | soft) :;; #(
      *)
        # In POSIX sh, ulimit -n is undefined. That's why the result is checked to see if it worked.
        # shellcheck disable=SC2039,SC3045
        ulimit -n "$MAX_FD" ||
            warn "Could not set maximum file descriptor limit to $MAX_FD"
    esac
fi

# Collect all arguments for the java command, stacking in reverse order:
#   * args from the command line
#   * the main class name
#   * -classpath
#   * -D...appname settings
#   * --module-path (only if needed)
#   * DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS, and GRADLE_OPTS environment variables.

# For Cygwin or MSYS, switch paths to Windows format before running java
if "$cygwin" || "$msys" ; then
    APP_HOME=$( cygpath --path --mixed "$APP_HOME" )

    JAVACMD=$( cygpath --unix "$JAVACMD" )

    # Now convert the arguments - kludge to limit ourselves to /bin/sh
    for arg do
        if
            case $arg in                                #(
              -*)   false ;;                            # don't mess with options #(
              /?*)  t=${arg#/} t=/${t%%/*}              # looks like a POSIX filepath
                    [ -e "$t" ] ;;                      #(
              *)    false ;;
            esac
        then
            arg=$( cygpath --path --ignore --mixed "$arg" )
        fi
        # Roll the args list around exactly as many times as the number of
        # args, so each arg winds up back in the position where it started, but
        # possibly modified.
        #
        # NB: a `for` loop captures its iteration list before it begins, so
        # changing the positional parameters here affects neither the number of
        # iterations, nor the values presented in `arg`.
        shift                   # remove old arg
        set -- "$@" "$arg"      # push replacement arg
    done
fi


# Add default JVM options here. You can also use JAVA_OPTS and GRADLE_OPTS to pass JVM options to this script.
DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS='"-Xmx64m" "-Xms64m"'

# Collect all arguments for the java command:
#   * DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS, and optsEnvironmentVar are not allowed to contain shell fragments,
#     and any embedded shellness will be escaped.
#   * For example: A user cannot expect ${Hostname} to be expanded, as it is an environment variable and will be
#     treated as '${Hostname}' itself on the command line.

set -- \
        "-Dorg.gradle.appname=$APP_BASE_NAME" \
        -jar "$APP_HOME/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar" \
        "$@"

# Stop when "xargs" is not available.
if ! command -v xargs >/dev/null 2>&1
then
    die "xargs is not available"
fi

# Use "xargs" to parse quoted args.
#
# With -n1 it outputs one arg per line, with the quotes and backslashes removed.
#
# In Bash we could simply go:
#
#   readarray ARGS < <( xargs -n1 <<<"$var" ) &&
#   set -- "${ARGS[@]}" "$@"
#
# but POSIX shell has neither arrays nor command substitution, so instead we
# post-process each arg (as a line of input to sed) to backslash-escape any
# character that might be a shell metacharacter, then use eval to reverse
# that process (while maintaining the separation between arguments), and wrap
# the whole thing up as a single "set" statement.
#
# This will of course break if any of these variables contains a newline or
# an unmatched quote.
#

eval "set -- $(
        printf '%s\n' "$DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS $JAVA_OPTS $GRADLE_OPTS" |
        xargs -n1 |
        sed ' s~[^-[:alnum:]+,./:=@_]~\\&~g; ' |
        tr '\n' ' '
    )" '"$@"'

exec "$JAVACMD" "$@"

```

`cmake/embed_spirv.cmake`:

```cmake
# Writes a C++ header with the given files (shaders, the window icon) as byte arrays:
#   cmake -DOUTPUT=out.h -DINPUTS="a.spv|b.spv|a.msl" -P embed_spirv.cmake
# Each array is named g_<file name with dots turned into underscores>,
# without the .spv extension (fixed.frag.spv -> g_fixed_frag,
# fixed.frag.msl -> g_fixed_frag_msl). MSL is source text: its array ends with
# a NUL that is not part of the shader. With MSL inputs the header also
# defines OPENCMR2_SHADERS_MSL.
string(REPLACE "|" ";" INPUTS "${INPUTS}")
set(content "// Generated from the compiled shaders. Do not edit.\n#pragma once\n\n")
foreach(input IN LISTS INPUTS)
    get_filename_component(name "${input}" NAME)
    string(REGEX REPLACE "\\.spv$" "" name "${name}")
    string(REPLACE "." "_" name "${name}")
    file(READ "${input}" hex HEX)
    if(input MATCHES "\\.msl$")
        string(APPEND hex "00")
        set(have_msl TRUE)
    endif()
    string(REGEX REPLACE "([0-9a-f][0-9a-f])" "0x\\1," bytes "${hex}")
    string(APPEND content "static const unsigned char g_${name}[] = {${bytes}};\n\n")
endforeach()
if(have_msl)
    string(APPEND content "#define OPENCMR2_SHADERS_MSL 1\n")
endif()
file(WRITE "${OUTPUT}" "${content}")

```

`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`:

```md
# OpenCMR2 architecture

OpenCMR2 is a native port of Colin McRae Rally 2.0 built from the
[CMR2Decomp](https://github.com/pablocpas/CMR2Decomp) decompilation. It runs on
SDL3 and the SDL GPU API (Vulkan, Metal) and needs the original game data.

## Layout

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `game/` | The decompiled game, synced from CMR2Decomp (`tools/sync_upstream.py`, last commit in `UPSTREAM`). |
| `src/port/` | The platform API the game calls: `types.h`, `sys.h`, `gfx.h`, `audio.h`, `input.h`, `movie.h`, `net.h`. Portable functions, compatibility types and disk-to-native layout conversion. |
| `src/platform/` | `main()`, window and event loop, time, files, configuration (SDL3). |
| `src/render/` | The SDL_GPU renderer behind `gfx.h`, and its shaders. |
| `src/audio/` | Mixer behind `audio.h` (SDL3 audio streams), WAV and MS-ADPCM decoding. |
| `src/input/` | Keyboard, mouse, joysticks, gamepads and force feedback (SDL3). |
| `src/video/` | Standalone Bink 1 (`BIKi`) video/audio decoder behind `movie.h`; queued sound uses the SDL3 mixer. No external codec library. See [VIDEO.md](VIDEO.md). |
| `src/net/` | Network sessions behind `net.h` (replaces DirectPlay). |
| `android/` | Android app (Gradle): game data import, the activity SDL runs the game in, on-screen controls. |
| `tests/` | Unit tests and the golden replay tests. |
| `tests/reference/` | Frozen recordings, comparison reports and provenance used by regression tests. |
| `tools/` | Source sync, layout generation, audits, captures and release packaging. |
| `docs/` | Guides and the generated raw-access report. |
| `build/` | Ignored build outputs, local captures, logs and toolchains. |

## How the game is ported

About 300 of the 3369 game functions call Win32 or DirectX; the rest is
platform-free logic. Those 300 are rewritten in place in `game/` against the
`src/port` API. They keep their `// FUNCTION: CMR2 0x...` annotation, so each
one can still be compared with the original, and get a `// PORT:` line that
says what changed. Game data structures that embedded DirectX types use our
types instead (`GfxTexture *` for `IDirectDrawSurface7 *`, `GfxTLVertex` for
`D3DTLVERTEX`). Structures used by raw-offset accesses or loaded from game data
must retain their required size and layout in the 32-bit build. Renderer-owned
descriptions can change when all their callers are adapted; layout checks for
the compatibility-sensitive structures are still required.

Everything else in `game/` is changed only for portability (inline assembly,
MSVC-only syntax, undefined behaviour) or for real bugs, so upstream syncs stay
easy. Keep those edits small and local.

The game source is compiled with `-include port/types.h`, which provides the
Win32 type names the decompilation uses (`BYTE`, `DWORD`, `BOOL`, `RECT`) with
Win32's sizes. It declares no Win32 functions.

## The renderer

CMR2 renders with Direct3D 7's fixed-function pipeline:

- one vertex format for 3D (FVF `0x2d2`: position, normal, diffuse,
  specular, two UV sets; 48 bytes), in vertex buffers the game fills itself,
  drawn with indexed triangle lists and strips;
- pre-transformed vertices for 2D (`GfxTLVertex`, the `D3DTLVERTEX` layout);
- hardware lighting with up to 8 lights (directional, point, spot), material
  colours taken from the vertex colour, ambient light;
- linear vertex/table fog;
- two texture stages (modulate, select, add-signed, bump env map), clamp or
  wrap, point/linear filtering with mipmaps;
- camera-space reflection vectors with a texture transform (car
  reflections), cube maps rendered at runtime;
- alpha blending, alpha test, depth test and write, culling.

`gfx.h` exposes exactly that model as state-setting calls on our own types
(`Gfx_SetTransform`, `Gfx_SetLight`, `Gfx_SetStage`, `Gfx_DrawIndexed`, ...).
The SDL_GPU backend turns the current state into a pipeline key and a uniform
block, and draws with an "uber" shader that reproduces the fixed-function
equations. Device enumeration, display-mode switching, lost surfaces and
COM disappear: the game asks for what it needs and the backend provides it.

The display modes offered to the game are the original 4:3 ones up to
1024x768 and the display's own aspect ratio from 540 lines up to the desktop
resolution. A new configuration starts at the display's aspect ratio at 720
lines (540 on Android): the game draws its menus, text and HUD in pixels for
640x480, so they shrink as the resolution grows, and higher modes are there
for a sharper 3D picture. As in SilentPatch, the projection keeps the
vertical view at any aspect ratio instead of stretching it, and the field of
view is configurable (`View_SetPlayerProjection`). Further rendering
improvements will be added one at a time, each behind an option, with the
original look as the default.

Textures: the game decodes TGA/DDS itself and writes pixels through
`Gfx_LockTexture`, using the pixel format the backend reports. The backend
offers 32-bit BGRA8, BC1 and BC3 (the DDS formats on the disc), and a dU/dV/L
bump format.

## Audio

The game uses DirectSound buffers: static samples, duplicated voices, 3D
voices (position, distances), frequency, volume in hundredths of a decibel,
pan, and a streamed music buffer refilled by regions. `audio.h` keeps those
semantics (sample, voice, stream) on our own types; `src/audio` mixes all
voices into one SDL3 audio stream and applies DirectSound's 3D attenuation.
WAV files and MS-ADPCM are decoded by our own code (the game used mmio and
ACM).

## Input

Key codes stay DirectInput scan codes (`DIK_*` values): the game stores them
in its binding tables and save files. `src/input` maps SDL scancodes to them.
Joysticks are read through SDL3 into a `DIJOYSTATE2`-like structure of our
own (axes, sliders, POVs, buttons). Controllers SDL knows the layout of are
presented as DirectInput showed an Xbox controller: sticks on X/Y and Rx/Ry,
buttons A, B, X, Y, LB, RB, Back, Start and the stick clicks, the D-pad as
POV 0. The triggers are Z and Rz, each read as DirectInput wheels report a
pedal: the maximum when released, the minimum when pressed fully, which is
what the game expects of a throttle and a brake on separate axes (DirectInput
put both triggers on Z, which kept them from being pressed together). Raw
axes that rest at their minimum, such as some wheels' pedals, are turned the
same way. A gamepad starts with throttle on the right trigger and brake on
the left (`PORT:` in `CInput::InitDetectedControllerSlot`). Force-feedback effects (constant, spring,
damper, friction, inertia) map to SDL haptic effects, with rumble as the
fallback on gamepads.

## Determinism and the golden tests

Vehicle physics uses integer fixed point. The reference build's target is to
reproduce the original simulation exactly, including input, scheduling, RNG
and the floating-point conversions used around the fixed-point core.

`tests/` checks the fixed-point helpers against the original assembly and tests
the existing scheduler's cadence, stored rates, cap, rebasing and wrap behaviour.
The optional `stage_probe` runs Finland through the real load/update path with
controlled clocks and recorded tick inputs. The corrected 500-update fixture
matches original + SilentPatch at six render cadences on Linux x86 and x86-64
and Windows x64 under Wine; see [PHYSICS_PARITY.md](PHYSICS_PARITY.md) for the
fields and timing contract. Shared RNG and presentation state are outside that
equivalence claim, and full-game equivalence is not yet established.
[BASELINE.md](BASELINE.md) covers capture and CPU profiling.

The compiler flags encode what the decompiled code relies on:

- `-fwrapv`: 16.16 fixed point overflows on purpose;
- `-fno-strict-aliasing`: the code reinterprets memory freely;
- `-msse2 -mfpmath=sse`: explicit float/double arithmetic. The audited original
  race used x87 53-bit precision; identical precision across drivers is not assumed;
- float-to-int conversions: the original TUs built with `/QIfist` round to
  nearest instead of truncating. Audited sites use `llrint`/`lrintf` explicitly,
  preserving the original narrowing after 64-bit conversion.

## Builds

- `linux-x86` (CMake preset): 32-bit x86, the reference build. Data
  structures have the original layout.
- `linux-x86-debug`: the same with AddressSanitizer and UBSan.
- `linux` and `linux-debug`: native Linux x86-64/ARM64, with optional sanitizers.
- `windows-x64` and `macos`: Windows x64 and macOS Apple silicon.

All target presets are built, tested and packaged in CI. Linux x86-64 and
Windows x64 under Wine have real-stage regression coverage; ARM64, macOS and
physical Windows gameplay still need validation. Remaining raw accesses are tracked in the
[generated audit](64bit-raw-access.md).

```

`docs/BASELINE.md`:

```md
# Stage baseline and CPU profiling

These tools record a real stage with controlled clocks and inputs, replay it
at different render cadences and measure CPU frame timings. They compare the
port with itself; the comparison with the original executable is in
[ORIGINAL_REFERENCE.md](ORIGINAL_REFERENCE.md) and
[PHYSICS_PARITY.md](PHYSICS_PARITY.md).

Normal play has no observer unless `OPENCMR2_PROFILE` is set. The fake clock and
keyboard overrides are enabled only by the separate `stage_probe` executable.

## Capture and playback

Build the 32-bit reference preset, then run:

```sh
python3 tools/stage_baseline.py run --data ~/cmr2game --output build/baseline-first
```

The driver loads Finland stage 1 through the real frontend and garage, with
fresh default settings, one default 4WD car and automatic transmission. It
isolates settings/saves in a temporary `XDG_DATA_HOME` for every run and uses
SDL's dummy video/audio drivers and the null graphics executor. Game-side
drawing, loading, audio decisions and the original tick body still run.

All runs bootstrap at the same 33 ms cadence and fixed Unix seed. After entering
race mode, the clock advances at the requested cadence using integer millisecond
samples. The clock sampling points are retained; the scheduler now evaluates
both rounded boundaries in double precision to prevent duplicate steps. The
variable cadence repeats 7/13/33/5/22/48/9/23 ms intervals.

The default 500 ticks cover approximately 20 simulation seconds: 125 countdown
ticks and 375 driving ticks. The script accelerates, steers left/right, coasts,
brakes and briefly applies the handbrake. Controls are assigned at the existing
boundary after device mapping and before the car update, indexed by simulation
tick. They are captured separately from the resulting car state.

The output includes:

- `reference.jsonl`: one explicit state record per completed tick, with no raw
  structure dumps, pointer values or padding. Fixed-point values retain their
  exact integers.
- `inputs.csv`: resolved digital/analog/shift controls before physics. `playback`
  reads this file at 60 FPS; all cross-cadence runs read the same file.
- `repeat.jsonl`: an independent run of the same scripted scenario. Both repeat
  and playback must match every recorded field.
- `fps-*.jsonl`: playback at 30/60/120/144/240 FPS and variable cadence.
- `*.frames.csv`: CPU timings on the real monotonic clock; virtual test time is
  never used for these measurements.
- `*.log` and `report.json`: scenario checks, binary/trace SHA-256, and the first
  differing tick/field, with a separate first car-state difference.

Use a new output directory for each capture; existing baselines are protected
against overwriting. Keep the same original assets when comparing builds. The
report identifies the probe binary, but does not fingerprint the whole asset
installation. It does not establish equivalence with an original Windows
executable.

To compare a later build against a saved trace:

```sh
python3 tools/stage_baseline.py compare \
    build/baseline-first/reference.jsonl build/baseline-next/reference.jsonl
```

`compare` returns 1 for a difference and 2 for invalid input. `run` fails when
repeat/playback is not identical or loading fails. Cross-cadence differences are
reported as baseline findings; add `--require-cadence` to make them failures.
Use `--ticks` or `--rates` to change the experiment. For direct probe use, set
`XDG_DATA_HOME` to a disposable directory:

```sh
XDG_DATA_HOME=/tmp/cmr2-probe SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy \
OPENCMR2_HEADLESS=1 build/linux-x86/tests/stage_probe \
    ~/cmr2game /tmp/stage.jsonl 60 500 build/baseline-first/inputs.csv
```

## Coverage and results

The trace covers selected fields of the ordered car: position/history, body
axes, velocities, controls, contact triangles and surfaces, suspension, wheel
loads/slip/torque, steering filter, engine/gear state, body damage grid,
per-part damage values/intensity, checkpoint indices and split times. It also
records the shared MSVC RNG state without advancing it.

It is a regression reference for this scenario, not a complete authoritative
state dump. AI, moving collision objects, every damage/debris node, device input
filters, full replay stream state, ghosts, multiple cars, pause/focus transitions,
resizing and race completion still need broader fixtures. Injecting resolved
controls deliberately bypasses hardware mapping/latency tests.

Validated on 2026-10-09 with the Linux x86 build and local original assets:

| Comparison | Recorded car/control/damage/checkpoint fields | Shared RNG |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 60 FPS repeat and recorded-input playback | Identical for all 500 ticks | Identical |
| 30, 120, 144, 240 FPS and variable cadence | Identical for all 500 ticks | Different from tick 0 |

At 60 FPS the probe also observed RNG changes in 704 race frames that performed
no simulation step; at 240 FPS there were 4304 such frames. These observations
establish frame-dependent use of the shared RNG, but do not identify all callers
or prove a resulting vehicle difference in this short scenario. Audit those
callers and their ownership before separating visual randomness or claiming
full cadence independence. Preserve these traces when implementing that boundary.

`car_scheduler` in CTest calls the existing scheduler directly. It covers ten
seconds at all five cadences and variable cadence, equal-rate car copying,
stored 50 Hz rates, zero elapsed time, multiple steps, the five-step cap and
discarded debt, menu/transition rebasing, and 32-bit millisecond wrap.

## Measure a normal session

```sh
OPENCMR2_PROFILE="$HOME/opencmr2-profile.csv" \
    build/linux-x86/src/opencmr2 --data ~/cmr2game
python3 tools/profile_summary.py ~/opencmr2-profile.csv
```

Close the game normally to write the CSV. Measurements are kept in memory,
capped at one million frames, so no CSV writes occur during live frame updates.
The profiler does not change the clock, controls, RNG or scheduling policy.

The CSV contains frame-start intervals, CPU time inside the frame callback,
total tick CPU time/count, and time in the presentation executor including CPU
submission/waits. Sound-slot servicing and event handling are outside callback
work time but can contribute to the next frame-start interval. Internal flushes
and readbacks remain part of callback/tick work; they are not separately timed.
The columns are observations of nested scopes, not separate budgets to add.

The summary prints median, p95, p99, maximum, frames above the chosen budget
and mean tick cost. Use `--budget-ms 6.944` for a 144 Hz budget and
`--from-frame N` to exclude startup/loading. Frame intervals measure callback
cadence, not actual monitor scanout. Blocking movies can occupy a single
callback with many internal presentations. Startup, menus and races should be
examined separately.

GPU execution time, actual display intervals and input-to-display latency are
not measured yet. Headless probe timings include trace overhead and no GPU;
use a normal session on the target machine to investigate real stutter. The
CSV path must have an existing parent directory. A crash/forced termination
does not flush the in-memory capture.

```

# Development workflow

Build requirements and platform presets are in the root [README](../README.md).
CI builds each supported platform using the same presets.

## Build and test

On Linux, run the native build and 32-bit reference build:

```sh
cmake --preset linux
cmake --build --preset linux
ctest --preset linux

cmake --preset linux-x86
cmake --build --preset linux-x86
ctest --preset linux-x86
```

The 32-bit build needs i386 libraries. On Ubuntu 24.04 (the CI environment),
SDL3 is built from source:

```sh
sudo dpkg --add-architecture i386
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install clang g++-multilib ninja-build glslang-tools pkg-config \
    libx11-dev:i386 libxext-dev:i386 libxrandr-dev:i386 libxcursor-dev:i386 \
    libxi-dev:i386 libxss-dev:i386 libxtst-dev:i386 libxkbcommon-dev:i386 \
    libwayland-dev:i386 wayland-protocols libegl1-mesa-dev:i386 \
    libasound2-dev:i386 libudev-dev:i386 libdbus-1-dev:i386
export PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR=/usr/lib/i386-linux-gnu/pkgconfig:/usr/share/pkgconfig
cmake --preset linux-x86 -DOPENCMR2_VENDORED_SDL=ON
```

On Fedora (`SDL3-devel.i686` is used when it is 3.4 or later):

```sh
sudo dnf install clang gcc-c++ glibc-devel.i686 libstdc++-devel.x86_64 \
    libstdc++-devel.i686 SDL3-devel.i686 ninja-build glslang
```

To include real-stage physics, runtime, lighting and movie regressions,
configure with your own original game data, then rebuild and test:

```sh
cmake --preset linux -DOPENCMR2_BINK_TEST_DATA_DIR="$HOME/cmr2game"
cmake --build --preset linux
ctest --preset linux
```

Use the same option for `linux-x86`. LAN game tests are registered for native
builds when game data is supplied; network tests require loopback UDP access.
See [PHYSICS_PARITY.md](PHYSICS_PARITY.md) and [BASELINE.md](BASELINE.md) for
the fixture scope and recording commands.

The `game_data_setup` test uses synthetic archive placeholders and simulated
desktop dialogs with SDL's dummy video driver. It covers first-run selection,
missing files, reading archives and writing saves under UTF-8 paths, remembered
settings, cancellation and a `Data` folder beside the executable. It also
checks selecting subfolders or parent folders, ambiguous installations and
symlink cycles on every CI platform, without original assets or a display
server.

## Source sync and generated files

`game/` follows CMR2Decomp; `UPSTREAM` records the imported commit.
Use `tools/sync_upstream.py`, inspect its changes and resolve any conflicts.
Port adaptations and tests must remain valid after a sync.

When compatibility-sensitive structures change, check the disk-layout header:

```sh
python3 tools/gen_disk_layouts.py --check
```

Regenerate it with `python3 tools/gen_disk_layouts.py` when needed and review
the diff. The raw-access audit requires `clang-devel` and writes its detailed
JSON and plugin caches under `build/`:

```sh
python3 tests/raw_access_audit.py --plugin
python3 tools/audit_raw_access.py --json build/raw-access-current.json \
  --markdown docs/64bit-raw-access.md --jobs 4
```

The Markdown audit is generated; update it with the tool. Individual reviews
in `tools/raw_access/reviewed.json` retain source guards and automatic evidence.

## Files to keep

- Keep guides in `docs/` and link them from its index. Results of a past
  investigation belong in the commit message, not in a new document.
- Keep frozen regression inputs, accepted comparisons and provenance in
  `tests/reference/`. Its recordings and audit logs support reproducible tests.
- Put temporary plans, logs, captures, build products and downloaded
  toolchains under `build/`. It is ignored by Git, as are `out/`, `dist/`,
  Python caches and local `CMakeUserPresets.json`.
- Never commit original game files. Release packages contain only the
  executable, its libraries and the licences.

Before committing, review `git status --short`, `git diff --check` and the staged
diff.
